display_name: Not able to drink or feed at all
note: Red flag = completely unable to drink/feed. poor_feeding/poor_appetite are milder — use a clarifying question ('Is the person completely unable to drink or feed anything?') before firing emergency, rather than auto-escalating every poor-appetite selection.

display_name: Confusion or unresponsiveness (not their normal self)
note: New confusion is itself a danger sign — escalating a 'confusion' selection to this red flag is clinically safe. lethargy (unusually sleepy) is escalate-safe in a child; clarify in an adult. This is the lead's cited near-miss (confusion -> altered_consciousness).

display_name: Struggling to breathe even while sitting still / at rest
note: Red flag is breathlessness AT REST. These near-misses can be mild-to-moderate — use a clarifying question ('Is it hard to breathe even when resting, not just on activity?') before firing emergency, to avoid over-triage. This is the lead's cited near-miss (difficulty_breathing -> breathlessness_at_rest). NB exertional_breathlessness deliberately excluded — it means 'with activity', not at rest.

display_name: Collapsed — cold, clammy skin, very weak or fainting
note: Non-specific near-misses — clarify for cold/clammy skin + collapse before escalating. Overlaps with 'shock'. circulatory_collapse is also a global red flag already covered by rf_006; ensure the picker path reaches it.

display_name: Too weak to stand, sit up, or feed without help
note: Prostration = cannot stand/sit/feed unaided. Escalate-safe for a child who cannot feed or sit; for an adult reporting general weakness, clarify ('Are they too weak to stand or sit up on their own?').

Generic 'bleeding' is the primary near-miss. Escalation depends on severity/volume — clarify whether bleeding is heavy or won't stop. vaginal_bleeding in pregnancy is separately an obstetric emergency; a minor nosebleed or trace bleeding_gums should NOT auto-fire emergency.

display_name: Blue or grey lips, tongue, or face
note: GAP: no direct cyanosis near-miss token exists in the picker. pallor (pale) may be colour-confused and difficulty_breathing often co-occurs, but neither is close. RECOMMEND adding an explicit 'Blue lips or face' picker option — as it stands caregivers have no accurate way to report this danger sign, so it is the most likely of the 12 to be missed even after this mapping.

display_name: Severe dehydration — sunken eyes, no tears, not passing urine, very drowsy
note: The picker's existing 'dehydration' (thirsty, dry mouth) is the milder near-miss and the main confusion risk. Clarify for severe signs (sunken eyes + drowsy or not passing urine) before firing emergency — do not auto-escalate every 'dehydration' selection.

display_name: Hard to wake, very drowsy, or not responding normally
note: Overlaps altered_consciousness. lethargy/confusion are escalate-safe in a child (both are IMCI danger signs); in an adult with mild drowsiness, clarify. Same near-miss tokens as altered_consciousness by design — the mobile engineer can route both red flags off the same picker selections.

display_name: Working very hard to breathe — nostrils flaring, chest pulling in, or can't speak a full sentence
note: chest_indrawing and fast_breathing_child are strong distress indicators — escalate-safe in a child. difficulty_breathing / fast_breathing in an adult: clarify for signs of real distress (flaring, indrawing, unable to complete sentences) before firing emergency.

display_name: Cold hands and feet, fast weak pulse, very drowsy or fainting
note: Overlaps circulatory_collapse — both are global red flags and the picker path should reach both. Near-misses are non-specific; clarify (cold peripheries + drowsy/fast pulse) before escalating a lone pallor or near_fainting selection.

display_name: Severe allergic reaction — face/throat swelling, widespread hives, and trouble breathing together
note: The red flag is these signs TOGETHER after an allergen/sting/food/drug exposure. Any single one alone is not anaphylaxis and should not auto-fire emergency — but hives or facial_swelling WITH difficulty_breathing or wheeze should escalate. RECOMMEND a combined-trigger rule (swelling/hives + breathing difficulty) rather than mapping each token individually.
